Definition: from G575 and G3068; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively):--wash (away).
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and both times about sins washed away. Ananias tells Paul in Acts 22:16 to arise, be baptized, and wash away his sins, calling on the name of the Lord, and Paul tells the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 6:11 that such were some of them — but ye are washed, ye are sanctified, ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: The washing is baptism's picture and the gospel's fact: the sins are gone, and the washed stand sanctified and justified.
